title: Northern Songs sues Maclen Music | 1970
content:
Northern Songs sued Maclen (Music) Ltd on 15 December 1970.

Dick James, the music publisher who founded Northern Songs with Beatles manager Brian Epstein, resigned from the company on 14 August. The Beatles had lost control of Northern Songs on 19 September 1969, when ATV took a 54% controlling stake in the company.

ATV had handed the management of Maclen Music, which handled Lennon and McCartney’s Beatles-era compositions for North America and the Philippines, to Don Kirshner’s Kirsher Entertainment Corporation. Maclen had previously been controlled by Northern Songs.

On this day Northern Songs issued a writ against Maclen, alleging that Lennon and McCartney were under contract until February 1973, and that, under their 1965 agreement, Maclen was not entitled to claim copyright on any of their Northern Songs-published compositions.

The lawsuit may have been prompted by Lennon’s recently-released debut solo album, John Lennon/Plastic Ono Band, which had been released on 11 December. The suit noted that the publishing credits for Lennon’s new songs were assigned to Maclen (Music) Ltd (UK), which was owned by Lennon and McCartney, and not Maclen Music, Inc.
